guitar.modelsText: Gibson Les Paul Standard ("Greeny", ex-Peter Green)
models: Gibson Les Paul Standard ("Greeny", ex-Peter Green)
guitar.notes: Confirmed and refined — Gary Moore's 1959 Les Paul "Greeny" (previously owned by Peter Green) is one of the most famous guitars in blues-rock history.

tone.target: sustaining Gary Moore lead with vocal vibrato and creamy drive
tone.profile: sustaining Gary Moore lead with vocal vibrato and creamy drive
tone.summary: A warm, singing signal chain utilizing a Boost/OD for initial drive, followed by an AC30-style amp simulation and a 4x12 cabinet, enhanced with Chorus and Digital Delay for sustain and vibrato.

rig.name: Gary Moore - The Messiah Will Come Again - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up hum and background noise.
Provide initial clean boost and sustain lift for lead lines.
blocks.gap: The Boost module is used to simulate the gentle push needed before a Plexi-style amp, avoiding heavy OD saturation.

alternatives.reason: If more grit than pure boost is desired.

blocks.purpose: Add creamy, singing mid-gain and sustain without heavy fuzz or modern crunch.
blocks.gap: Red Haze is chosen for its vintage character, simulating the desired 'creamy drive' while avoiding the harshness of pure distortion.

alternatives.reason: A slightly cleaner alternative if Red Haze is too aggressive.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the classic British Plexi/Marshall voicing for a warm, singing lead tone.
blocks.gap: The AC30 TB is ideal for capturing the 'Plexi' sound and warmth requested, while avoiding the JCM-800 edge.

alternatives.reason: A slightly more aggressive British option.

blocks.purpose: Provide the classic British 4x12 voicing required for lead tones.
Enhance the 'wide vibrato' and give the lead tone a singing, ethereal quality.
blocks.gap: Chorus is used here to simulate controlled pitch modulation/vibrato, which is key for Gary Moore's style.

alternatives.reason: If a more rhythmic vibrato is preferred over a sustained wash.

blocks.purpose: Add a touch of delay to enhance sustain and space the lead lines.
Add subtle depth and roundness to the overall tone without sounding ambient.
blocks.gap: Room reverb provides a natural, non-overpowering sense of space suitable for lead guitar work.

alternatives.reason: If a more defined, metallic echo is desired.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism for a more authentic British lead tone.

proposals.reason: The AC30/Plexi sound needs a dedicated Marshall-voiced cabinet to ground the tone.
